'''''Libertia''''' is a [[genus]] of [[monocotyledon]]ous plants in the family [[Iridaceae]], first described as a genus in 1824.<ref name=":0">[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/6720194#page/133/mode/1up Sprengel, Curt Polycarp Joachim 1824.  Systema Vegetabilium, editio decima sexta 1: 127] in Latin</ref> It is native to South America, Australia, [[New Guinea]], and New Zealand. Eight species are [[endemic (ecology)|endemic]] to New Zealand.<ref name=k>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=323217 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref name="blanchon">{{cite journal | last1 = Blanchon | first1 = D.J. |display-authors=etal  | year = 2002 | title = A taxonomic revision of ''Libertia'' (Iridaceae) in New Zealand | journal = New Zealand Journal of Botany | volume = 40 | issue = 3| pages = 437–456 | doi=10.1080/0028825x.2002.9512805| bibcode = 2002NZJB...40..437B | s2cid = 83634447 }}</ref><ref name=gn>{{cite web|title=Census of vascular plants of Papua New Guinea|url=http://plantnet.rbgsyd.nsw.gov.au/cgi-bin/PNGcensus.pl?fam=&gen=Libertia&sp=&infr=&group=|access-date=2010-01-01}}</ref>

''Libertia'' is made up of [[herbaceous]] or [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennials]] growing from short [[rhizome]]s,<ref name=":0" /> with simple, linear or narrowly lanceolate basal leaves which are often green but may be red, orange, or yellow under direct sunlight.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://igpsblogs.wordpress.com/tag/stephen-butler/|title=Stephen Butler {{!}} IGPS Blog|website=igpsblogs.wordpress.com|language=en|access-date=2017-03-12}}</ref> The showy white or blue trimerous flowers are open in spring and are followed by [[Capsule (botany)|capsules]] opening by three valves which contain the numerous seeds.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Goldblatt; Henrich; Keating|first=Peter; James; Richard|year=1989|title=Seed morphology of Sisyrinchium (Iridaceae-Sisyrinchieae) and its allies|journal=Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden|volume=76 | issue = 4 |pages=1109–1117|jstor=2399695|doi=10.2307/2399695}}</ref>

The genus was named after the Belgian botanist [[Marie-Anne Libert]]<ref>{{cite book| title=CRC World Dictionary of Grasses, Common Names, Scientific Names, Eponyms, Synonyms, and Etymology | first=Umberto |last=Quattrocchi| volume=1 |pages=124 | publisher=Taylor and Francis |year=2006 | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8ieqQs7hIREC&q=libertia&pg=PA1224| isbn=9781420003222 }}</ref> (1782–1865) (also referred to as Anne-Marie Libert).<ref name=Goldblatt2008>{{cite book |author1=Manning, John |author2=Goldblatt, Peter |title=The Iris Family: Natural History & Classification |publisher=Timber Press |location=Portland, Oregon|pages=215–16 |year=2008|isbn=978-0-88192-897-6}}</ref>

The species ''Libertia chilensis'' has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name = RHSPF>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/23471/i-Libertia-chilensis-i/Details | title = RHS Plantfinder - ''Libertia chilensis''
| access-date= 22 March 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf | title = AGM Plants - Ornamental | date = July 2017 | page = 60 | publisher = Royal Horticultural Society | access-date = 14 March 2018}}</ref>

== Cytology ==

''Libertia'' has a high rate of [[polyploid]]y, with 9/11 of assessed species confirmed as [[polyploid]] and only 3 confirmed as [[Diploidy|diploid]].<ref name="blanchon" /> This is not unprecedented, with [[polyploid]]y being a common feature in the tribe [[Sisyrinchieae]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Goldblatt; Takei|first=P.; M.|year=1997|title=Chromosome cytology of Iridaceae-patterns of variation, determination of ancestral base numbers, and modes of karyotype change|journal=Annals of the Missouri Botanical Garden|volume=85 | issue = 2 |pages=285–304|doi=10.2307/2400005|jstor=2400005|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/part/26213 }}</ref> The uniform base number of x=19<ref name=":1" /> is, however, defining within the tribe. This base number is not found elsewhere in the tribe and only [[Diplarrena|''Diplarrhena'']] and ''[[Solenomelus]]'' have uniform base numbers intragenerically.<ref name=":1" />

All [[New Zealand]] [[Endemism|endemic]] species of ''Libertia'' are diploid,  [[Polyploid|hexaploid]] or [[Polyploid|dodecaploid]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Blanchon; Weaver|first=D.J.; J.S.|year=2009|title=Libertia flaccidifolia (Iridaceae), a new species from Mt. Tamahunga, Northland, New Zealand|journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany|volume=47|issue=3|pages=317–324|doi=10.1080/00288250909509812|bibcode=2009NZJB...47..317B |s2cid=86060799}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last=Blanchon|first=D.J.|year=2000|title=Chromosome numbers in the genus Libertia|journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany|volume=38 | issue = 2 |pages=245–250|doi=10.1080/0028825x.2000.9512681|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal|last=Hair; Beuzenberg; Pearson|first=J.B.; E.J.; B.|year=1967|title=Contributions to a chromosome atlas of the New Zealand flora - 9. Miscellaneous families|journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany|volume=5|pages=185–196|doi=10.1080/0028825x.1967.10428739|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal|last=Moore|first=L.B.|year=1967|title=The New Zealand species of Libertia (Iridaceae)|journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany|volume=5 | issue = 2 |pages=255–275|doi=10.1080/0028825x.1967.10428745|doi-access=free|bibcode=1967NZJB....5..255M }}</ref><ref name="blanchon" /> while these levels of [[ploidy]] have not been found outside [[New Zealand]]. [[Polyploid]]y is more prevalent in [[New Zealand]] species across all botanical taxa<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Rendle; Murray|first=H.; B.G.|year=1989|title=Chromosome relationships and breeding barriers in New Zealand species of Ranunculus|journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany|volume=27|issue=3|pages=437–444|doi=10.1080/0028825x.1989.10414124|doi-access=free|bibcode=1989NZJB...27..437R }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Murray; Cameron; Standring|first=B.G.; E.K.; L.S.|year=1992|title=Chromosome numbers, karyotypes, and nuclear DNA variation in Pratia Gaudin (Lobeliaceae)|journal=New Zealand Journal of Botany|volume=30|issue=2|pages=181–187|doi=10.1080/0028825x.1992.10412897|doi-access=free|bibcode=1992NZJB...30..181M }}</ref> and this has been attributed as a relic of glacial [[Refugium (population biology)|refugia]] during [[Ice age|glacial maximums]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=McQueen|first=D.R.|year=1992|title=Disjunction of tree species in mountain forests, southern North Island, New Zealand: a review of paleobotanical evidence|journal=Pacific Science|volume=46 | issue = 2 |pages=269–275}}</ref>
